Consulting

180 Degrees Consulting

Junior Consultant

Sep 2026 to present · Gainesville, FL

At 180 Degrees Consulting at UF, I work with We Are Neutral, a nonprofit that helps businesses measure and reduce their carbon footprint. My part is finding potential sponsors and deciding who to approach first.

  • I’m evaluating more than 25 prospective partners across three industries. The goal is to cut sponsor research time by 27%.
  • I’m comparing five peer organizations’ partnership models and prioritizing 10 partners for the client’s leadership team. The proposed sponsorship tiers represent up to $40,000 in potential funding.

Clinical research

Intelligent Clinical Care Center

Research Assistant

May 2026 to present · University of Florida, Gainesville, FL

I helped UF Health Shands clinicians decide which ICU delirium-risk models to test next.

  • I compared models across 12-, 24-, and 36-hour windows. Finding the five most predictive clinical variables helped narrow the next round of validation from eight configurations to three.
  • I made charts comparing six clinical measures for Dr. Rashidi and the clinical team. The team cut lower-priority validation work by about 23%.

Methods

  • Model comparison
  • Data visualization
  • Clinical metrics

Applied machine learning

Emotion-Based Music Recommender

Facial expression to Spotify recommendations

Public GitHub project

I connected a webcam-based facial-expression classifier to Spotify. A listener can request one track or build a playlist using the detected expression and their recent listening history.

  • OpenCV captures the webcam frame. A Keras classifier supplies an expression label, and the app uses recent Spotify listening to shape the recommendation.
  • I built a Tkinter interface for choosing playlist length, previewing songs, and reviewing locally recorded predictions. The repository includes the FER2013 training notebook.

Source code

Analytics

E-Commerce Sales Dashboard

Four ways to examine retail performance

Public GitHub project

I wrote a Python analysis that looks at the same retail sales data from four angles. Monthly totals show when demand changed, while product, category, and region breakdowns show which parts of the business drove it.

  • The script reads an order-level CSV and aggregates sales by calendar month, region, product category, and individual product.
  • It exports charts and a text summary. The top-products view ranks the ten highest-grossing products, giving a sales team a short list to investigate.

Source code

Tools

  • Python
  • pandas
  • Matplotlib

Analytics

Spotify Listening Trends

An analysis of 1,000 simulated plays

Public GitHub project

I used a simulated listening log to explore how artist rankings and listening activity change with the time of day and month. The CSV and the analysis script are both in the repository.

  • The included file has 1,000 plays dated January through March 2025. March has 349 plays, January 343, and February 308.
  • The Weeknd appears on 111 rows, the highest count. The script also reports the leading genre and busiest listening hour. These figures describe the sample dataset.

A weekly planner with focus and break timers

Public GitHub project

  • The same interface includes a 25-minute focus timer and a five-minute break timer.

Full-stack development

Real-Time Chat

Live messages with persistent history

Public GitHub project

I built a chat app that pairs live message delivery with a persistent conversation history. The React client can display a new message immediately and reload earlier messages later.

  • Socket.IO handles live updates between clients. Express exposes a REST endpoint for message history, and MongoDB stores the messages.
  • The repository contains the packaged client and server and a screenshot of the conversation interface.

Sudoku Interface

Menus, difficulty selection, and a 9 × 9 board

Public GitHub project

I used Pygame to build the interface for a Sudoku prototype. The project focuses on how a player moves between the menu, difficulty selection, and game board.

  • The board draws thicker lines around each 3 × 3 block. Shared button functions handle the menu and screen transitions.
  • The source covers the game screens and navigation. The reset control currently logs the action, and the prototype does not generate or solve puzzles.
